review.title: Comparing strings in Java
review.body: How should two `String` values be compared for equal content in Java?
review.explanation: `==` may appear to work for interned literals but fails for strings created at runtime. Use `Objects.equals(a, b)` to handle null safely.

review.title: Availability zones
review.body: Why deploy instances across multiple availability zones?

options.text: To reduce latency to all users worldwide
To survive the failure of a single data centre within a region

review.explanation: Use multiple regions for disaster recovery or global latency; multi-AZ protects against data-centre outages.

review.title: Memoisation vs tabulation

options.text: Tabulation is top-down recursion with a cache
Tabulation fills a table bottom-up iteratively; memoisation caches results of top-down recursive calls

review.explanation: Tabulation avoids recursion depth limits and often allows rolling-array space optimisation; memoisation computes only the states actually reached.

review.title: Why String is immutable
review.body: Which is a benefit of `String` being immutable in Java?

options.text: Strings can be modified in place faster
Strings can be safely shared, cached (string pool) and used as HashMap keys and across threads
It uses less memory when concatenating in loops

review.explanation: Repeated concatenation creates many objects; StringBuilder avoids that.

review.title: Discriminated unions
review.body: Given `type Shape = { kind: 'circle'; r: number } | { kind: 'square'; side: number }`, how does TypeScript know `shape.r` exists inside `if (shape.kind === 'circle')`?

options.text: Checking the literal discriminant property narrows the union to the matching member

review.explanation: Add an exhaustive `switch` with a `never` check in the default branch so adding a new variant produces a compile error where it is not handled.

review.title: Mutable default arguments
review.codeSnippet:
def add(item, items=[]):
    items.append(item)
    return items

add(1)
print(add(2))
review.explanation: Default values are evaluated once at function definition. Use `items=None` and create a new list inside the function.

review.title: GC and Dispose
review.body: True or false: the garbage collector automatically calls `Dispose()` on unreachable objects that implement `IDisposable`.

options.explanation: The GC only runs finalizers; Dispose must be called explicitly.

review.explanation: The GC knows nothing about `IDisposable`. It may run a **finalizer** (`~ClassName`) on objects that declare one, at an unpredictable time. The dispose pattern calls `GC.SuppressFinalize(this)` in `Dispose` so the finalizer is skipped when cleanup already happened.

review.title: Authentication before authorization

options.text: It is just a convention with no effect
Authorization evaluates HttpContext.User, which authentication middleware populates from the request credentials
Authorization middleware starts the authentication handlers itself
Because UseAuthorization registers the JWT handler

review.explanation: Authentication answers *who are you?* and sets `HttpContext.User`. Authorization answers *are you allowed?* by evaluating policies against that principal. Placing authorization first means every user is anonymous at evaluation time.

review.title: Quicksort worst case
review.body: What is quicksort's worst-case time complexity and when does it occur?

options.text: O(n²), when pivots repeatedly split the array very unevenly (e.g. first-element pivot on sorted input)

review.explanation: Randomised or median-of-three pivots make this unlikely. Introsort (used by .NET's Array.Sort and C++ std::sort) switches to heap sort when recursion gets too deep.

review.title: The GIL
review.body: In standard CPython builds, what does the Global Interpreter Lock imply for CPU-bound code?

options.text: Threads run Python bytecode truly in parallel on all cores
Only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time, so CPU-bound work should use multiprocessing (or native extensions)

options.explanation: Threads release the GIL during blocking I/O.

review.explanation: Threads still help I/O-bound work. CPython 3.13 introduced an experimental free-threaded build without the GIL, but the default build keeps it.
